Subject: Zenith Health: Hosting mode recommendation & sizing ask

Hi Helen / Procurement team —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Following up with a short summary of the hosting options we discussed and a few data points we need to size a proposed Dedicated vs Private deployment for your regulated workloads. I've attached a one-pager with the tradeoffs.

Quick recap: we can provide (1) a Dedicated reserved pool with network isolation and SLA-backed capacity, or (2) a Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) for air-gapped or highly regulated needs. Both support our model catalog and audit logs; they differ on latency, procurement path, and lead time.

What we need from you to finalize a recommended footprint:
- Typical and peak concurrent requests (RPS) for inference (or expected active conversations).
- Average/median sequence length per request (tokens) and P95 expected length.
- 99th percentile latency target (p95/p99) for text generation endpoints.
- Data residency / region constraint (US / EU / APAC) and whether data must be fully air-gapped.
- Retention period for logs & store-of-record (days).
- Target go-live date and pilot length.

If you prefer, we can propose two options (pilot + scale) in a short deck.

Next steps: can you reply with the numbers above? If helpful, we can run a sizing quick model with your sample traffic (CSV).

Attach: zenith_hosting_one-pager.pdf (2 pages)

Thanks,

Stephanie —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications and initial numbers from our side:

- Compliance: We are HIPAA-covered and need evidence of SOC 2 + HIPAA BAAs. In addition, some datasets must never leave our US environment (US-only). Air-gapped is preferable for PHI processing, but if we can get VPC-private with customer-managed KMS and strict egress locking, that may be acceptable.
- Traffic: pilot expected to be ~25 RPS (inference requests) with peaks of 80 RPS during business hours. Production target after Q1 2027: 200–250 RPS sustained with spikes to 400 RPS.
- Request size: average 350 tokens / request; p95 ~1,200 tokens. Most requests are chat-like with some reranking flows that are shorter.
- Latency: p95 generation latency target is <= 400ms for core workflows; some non-critical flows can tolerate 1s.
- Retention: logs/store-of-record retention required 365 days; audit logs must be exportable to our SIEM.
- Timeline: procurement expects a paper-signed SOW by end of December 2026; pilot ideally in early January (2–3 week pilot).

We'd like a ballpark cost and a lead-time estimate (how long until a Dedicated pool can be provisioned vs Private install). Also please confirm what parts of the stack are customer-managed in the Private option (network, KMS, backups).

Thanks,
Helen Zhao

Stephanie / team —

I ran a quick sizing exercise based on Helen's numbers. High-level findings below; spreadsheet attached with assumptions and headroom scenarios (zenith_sizing_spreadsheet.csv).

Option A — Dedicated (recommended for performance + faster time-to-live):
- Pilot config (2-week PoC): 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed precision / 8-bit quant) in a reserved pool, autoscale + burst to 6 GPUs for peaks. Estimated sustained throughput: ~180–220 RPS for 350-token average with p95 ~350ms assuming batching and KV caching; spikes to 400 RPS covered by burst.
- Production: 8x A100-equivalent reserved (predictable throughput, isolation via tenant routing). Provides ~400–500 RPS sustained with headroom for growth.
- Lead time: Provisioning a Dedicated pool (in-hosted region) ~2–3 weeks after contract; can be faster (1 week) with priority allocation.
- Pros: SLA-backed latency, easier to meet p95 target, simpler procurement path (monthly reserved).
- Cons: higher base monthly cost vs minimal Private install; less control over KMS if customer wants HSM (we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations on Dedicated but not full HSM in every region).

Option B — Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Pilot config: single-customer VPC with 3x A100-equivalent GPUs (on our managed private control plane) — expected throughput ~120–160 RPS, p95 ~420–600ms depending on network egress.
- Production: scaled private cluster 6x A100-equivalent (or on-prem footprint mirrored across two racks) — throughput similar to Dedicated but requires longer lead time for air-gapped/on-prem hardware procurement.
- Lead time: VPC in a cloud region ~2–4 weeks; on-prem or air-gapped deployment 6–10 weeks (hardware lead times + installation).
- Pros: maximum data residency and control, tighter compliance posture for PHI.
- Cons: longer lead time, higher operational involvement, higher one-time engineering effort for on-prem.

Security/compliance notes:
- We can provide SOC 2 and HIPAA support docs; BAA is standard for enterprise customers.
- Audit/log export: both modes support streaming audit logs to customer SIEM via secure delivery; retention can be configured to meet 365d.

Recommendation summary: For Zenith's timeline (SOW by Dec, pilot Jan) and target throughput, Dedicated reserved pool with strict VPC peering + customer-managed KMS gives the best balance: meets latency targets, faster provisioning, and satisfies most compliance requirements. If Zenith requires a fully air-gapped PHI path for a subset of workloads, we should propose a hybrid: Dedicated for non-PHI + Private on-prem for PHI flows.

Next steps from our side:
1) Stephanie: draft a two-option commercial (Dedicated vs Hybrid) with ballpark pricing and SLA differentials for procurement.
2) Marissa/Karthik: finalize sizing spreadsheet and estimated monthly committed cost.
3) Ops: confirm lead-time calendar for Dedicated capacity in us-east and a VPC peering checklist.

Attach: zenith_sizing_spreadsheet.csv (CSV with assumptions)

Best,

Helen —

Thanks for the details and thanks Marissa for the sizing work. Quick consolidated recommendation and asks so procurement has what it needs for SOW routing: 

High-level recommendation: Dedicated Reserved Pool + VPC peering (Primary) with Hybrid fallback for PHI-heavy flows
- Pilot (Jan, 2–3 weeks): Deploy a 4x A100-equivalent Dedicated cluster with autoscale to 6 GPUs for load spikes. Includes customer-managed KMS integration, SOC2 docs, and audit log streaming to Zenith SIEM.
- Production (post-pilot): Convert to 8x A100-equivalent reserved capacity with SLA (p95 latency commitment) and monthly committed billing.
- If Zenith requires fully air-gapped handling for PHI, propose a hybrid: Dedicated for general inference, on-prem Private for PHI with sync/ingest boundaries. This minimizes procurement lead time and keeps critical PHI in a compliant boundary.

Ballpark commercial (order-of-magnitude to inform procurement):
- Pilot: setup fee + monthly equivalent for 4x GPUs: roughly $30k–$45k (pilot month cost and setup, dependent on quantization profile).
- Production (8x reserved): committed monthly ~$80k–$110k (includes SLA and monitoring). Exact pricing will depend on term length and burst allowances; we can refine in a commercial proposal.

Lead times: Dedicated pool in us-east ~1–3 weeks after PO; VPC/private install for on-prem air-gapped ~6–10 weeks.

Deliverables attached: Redwood recommendation brief and the sizing spreadsheet. If this direction matches Zenith's internal risk posture, can Procurement share a copy of the SOW template or preferred contract amendments? We'll prepare a short commercial and an SOW draft for legal review.

Proposed next meeting: Tue, Nov 23 10:00 AM ET (30 min) to review the commercial and SOW checklist. Let me know if that works; we can also run a quick tech deep-dive with Marissa and Karthik earlier.
